title: Checks for HTTPS requests that disable SSL certificate checks.
summary: If SSL certificates are not verified, an attacker could perform a "man in the middle" attack by intercepting and modifying traffic between the client and server. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.213.
message_templates: Probable use of `{}` call with `verify=False` disabling SSL certificate checks

title: Checks for function calls with parameters that indicate the use of insecure SSL and TLS protocol versions.
summary: Several highly publicized exploitable flaws have been discovered in all versions of SSL and early versions of TLS. The following versions are considered insecure, and should be avoided: - SSL v2 - SSL v3 - TLS v1 - TLS v1.1 Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.2.0.
message_templates: Call made with insecure SSL protocol: `{}`

title: Checks for function definitions with default arguments set to insecure SSL and TLS protocol versions.
summary: Several highly publicized exploitable flaws have been discovered in all versions of SSL and early versions of TLS. The following versions are considered insecure, and should be avoided: - SSL v2 - SSL v3 - TLS v1 - TLS v1.1 Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.2.0.
message_templates: Argument default set to insecure SSL protocol: `{}`

title: Checks for calls to ssl.wrap_socket() without an ssl_version.
summary: This method is known to provide a default value that maximizes compatibility, but permits use of insecure protocols. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.2.0.

title: Checks for uses of cryptographic keys with vulnerable key sizes.
summary: Small keys are easily breakable. For DSA and RSA, keys should be at least 2048 bits long. For EC, keys should be at least 224 bits long. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.2.0.
message_templates: {} key sizes below {} bits are considered breakable

title: Checks for uses of the yaml.load function.
summary: Running the yaml.load function over untrusted YAML files is insecure, as yaml.load allows for the creation of arbitrary Python objects, which can then be used to execute arbitrary code. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.212.
message_templates: Probable use of unsafe loader `{}` with `yaml.load`. Allows instantiation of arbitrary objects. Consider `yaml.safe_load`.
Probable use of unsafe `yaml.load`. Allows instantiation of arbitrary objects. Consider `yaml.safe_load`.

title: Checks for uses of policies disabling SSH verification in Paramiko.
summary: By default, Paramiko checks the identity of the remote host when establishing an SSH connection. Disabling the verification might lead to the client connecting to a malicious host, without the client knowing. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.2.0.
message_templates: Paramiko call with policy set to automatically trust the unknown host key

title: Checks for uses of SNMPv1 or SNMPv2.
summary: The SNMPv1 and SNMPv2 protocols are considered insecure as they do not support encryption. Instead, prefer SNMPv3, which supports encryption. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.218.
message_templates: The use of SNMPv1 and SNMPv2 is insecure. Use SNMPv3 if able.

title: Checks for uses of the SNMPv3 protocol without encryption.
summary: Unencrypted SNMPv3 communication can be intercepted and read by unauthorized parties. Instead, enable encryption when using SNMPv3. Ruff takes this rule from flake8-bandit and made it stable in v0.0.218.
message_templates: You should not use SNMPv3 without encryption. `noAuthNoPriv` & `authNoPriv` is insecure.
